source.title: Refusal-Gated Decoding: Preserving Refusal Behavior Under High-Temperature Sampling
source.authors: Phillip Howard; Xin Su; Allen G. Roush; Manikandan Ravikiran; Run-Yan Tan; Amir Abdullah

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether changing decoding temperature changes refusal behavior, using refusal-preservation and non-refusal rates rather than the original fine-tuning or KL-divergence methods.
record.gate_note: Tests direct high-temperature sampling, including temperature-related changes in refusal outcomes. It does not test fine-tuning, compliant prefilling, adversarial suffixes, or whether aligned-versus-base per-token KL is concentrated at the start. Results for the paper's own RGD and RGD-residual methods are not rows because they report performance of a new decoding method rather than an effect of the claim's intervention itself.
record.test_reason: The paper's own direct-sampling control measures how often a decoding change (raising temperature to T = 1.0–2.0) turns greedy refusals into coherent non-refusals. It does this across seven aligned models and three benchmarks. That bears on V4's decoding-change part. The RGD and RGD-residual results are the paper's own method and are correctly not rows.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors report that direct sampling at T = 2.0 keeps only 91.9% of greedy refusals on average. RGD raises this to 98.3% while leaving at least 98.1% of greedy non-refusals on unchanged high-temperature sampling, at 1.022–1.043x median latency. They conclude that high-temperature diversity need not erode refusal behavior.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates decoding temperature and refusal-gated decoding, not fine-tuning or aligned-versus-base KL measurement; includes a two-token SafeDecoding comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: Refusal preservation varies by model and dataset; higher temperature increases the any-of-ten coherent non-refusal rate for each tested model. Llama uses p-less sampling rather than its shipped top-p setting.

fits_no_version.finding: For Qwen2.5-7B, refusal-associated SAE features are active at fewer of the first four response positions at T = 2 than at T = 1; frequency-matched control features do not change.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: High-temperature samples weaken internal refusal-feature activity at the response opening.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the logit lens, 'sorry' first becomes Qwen2.5's top token at block 22–23 of 28.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal wording becomes the leading prediction only in late layers.

record.code_released: not stated; authors say they will make code publicly available
record.problems: Refusal outcomes are judged by a 2-of-3 LLM panel; the human check covers 50 responses. The principal measure is preservation of each model's own greedily refused prompts, not a general harmful-compliance rate. Direct-sampling results are ten-seed means, and outcomes vary by model and dataset.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; 35 rows recorded, below the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: No aligned-vs-base per-token KL. The first-tokens idea is only cited from Qi et al. as motivation.
Compliant prefilling, adversarial suffixes, and decoding changes other than temperature/truncation.
No weight or rank localization tested.
No test of data or objective as the cause of shallowness.
No deepening training. RGD is an inference-time wrapper, not alignment training.

missing.what: Greedy-refusal preservation of direct sampling at T = 1.0 and T = 1.5 per model and dataset, showing the dose-response with temperature
Refusal rate on refuse-labeled prompts, greedy vs direct sampling at T = 2.0 (e.g. Qwen3.8 WildJailbreak 88.30% to 78.68%; Llama JBB 92% to 86.30%). This is a dataset-label harmful-refusal measure
Qwen2.5 harmful-labeled refusal cohort: coherent non-refusal share of samples rises 4.3%, 5.6%, 6.2% from T = 1.0 to 2.0
Harmful-sample rate among harmless greedy non-refusals at T = 2.0 is 0.72–1.40%
43% of T = 2 samples on greedily refused prompts leave the greedy opening within four tokens

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Its measure is preservation of each model's own greedy refusals, not harmful compliance as such: the cohorts include benign XSTest over-refusals, and the loss counts degenerate outputs. The 2-of-3 judge panel matched human majority labels on 45 of 50 responses. Section 3 explicitly assumes Qi et al.'s first-few-tokens finding as motivation for a short greedy probe. The A-row baselines for A02–A07 were taken from Table 7's T = 1.5 column.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful fine-tuning and the number of fine-tuning examples.
Benign fine-tuning and its effects on harmful compliance.
The study does not measure per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models.
Tests temperature changes; does not test compliant prefilling, adversarial suffixes, or other decoding changes beyond the reported SafeDecoding comparison.
Does not test whether a small set of model weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Does not test whether training data or the training objective causes safety to be shallow.
Does not train safety to be deeper or test whether such training holds up.

relationships.condition: Direct high-temperature sampling, seven aligned models, pooled over JBB, XSTest and WildJailbreak, prompt-level any-of-ten measure
relationships.reason: In every model, the share of greedily refused prompts with a coherent non-refusal among ten samples rises with temperature, reaching 14.50–38.17% at T = 2.0 (A01–A07). Preservation falls below the greedy cohort in every cell (D01–D21).
relationships.display_finding: In every model, the share of greedily refused prompts with a coherent non-refusal among ten samples rose with temperature, reaching 14.50–38.17% at T = 2.0, and refusal preservation fell below the greedy level in every tested setting.

relationships.condition: Per-sample refusal preservation at T = 2.0 under direct sampling, all models and datasets
relationships.reason: Temperature alone only partly defeats refusal. It preserves 83.98–97.87% of greedy refusals per sample, and the losses include degenerate outputs and benign XSTest over-refusals (D01–D21). Llama needed p-less sampling to stay coherent at high temperature.
relationships.display_finding: Temperature alone only partly defeats refusal, preserving 83.98–97.87% of greedy refusals per sample. The losses include degenerate outputs and benign XSTest over-refusals, and Llama needed p-less sampling to stay coherent.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Direct high-temperature sampling at T = 2.0 across the seven tested models and three benchmark datasets
reader_labels.reason: Refusal preservation is below the greedy-refusal cohort baseline in every setting (D01–D21), and the share with a coherent non-refusal in any of ten samples rises from T = 1.0 to T = 2.0 for each model (A01–A07).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Direct high-temperature sampling and the SafeDecoding comparison in the reported settings
reader_labels.reason: The effect is not near-total removal: direct sampling preserves 83.98%–97.87% of greedy refusals at T = 2.0, while SafeDecoding preserves 98.02%–99.71% on Llama (D01–D21, SD01–SD03).
